parts.heading: Understanding Reparenting
parts.job: Orients a new reader: what reparenting is, why it is hard to begin, how the path usually unfolds, and why the author trusts it. Anything that explains the idea, its logic or its stages, or builds motivation and credibility before the reader tries it, serves this part.

parts.heading: Safety and Readiness
parts.job: Decides whether, when and how fast to start. It covers the reader's current state and risks: going in gently, a body or mind that is overwhelmed, danger from people or from oneself, and crisis. Anything that screens for or guards against harm before or at the start of the work belongs here.

parts.heading: Building Your Inner Adult
parts.job: Builds the caring grown-up inside the reader that the rest of the practice depends on, one function at a time (protecting, loving, guiding), including how to borrow those functions from others or from ideals while they are still weak. Anything about forming, strengthening or borrowing the adult side, or about earning the child's trust, serves this part.

parts.heading: Practicing With Your Little One
parts.job: The hands-on, repeatable methods for actually relating to the inner child in a session or a day: ways to make contact, hear the child, work with feelings and thoughts, and open and close the session. Anything that tells the reader what to do or try with the child, as opposed to who to become or what to watch out for, serves this part.

parts.heading: Discovering and Healing Old Patterns
parts.job: Goes below the surface once contact exists: seeing where inherited habits of distrust, shame, harshness or blame came from, and reworking painful memories and the inner critic with more understanding, forgiveness and healthier responses. Anything about the origin and repair of past hurts and learned patterns belongs here.

parts.heading: When the Practice Gets Difficult
parts.job: Troubleshooting for a practice that feels fake, empty, stuck, obsessive, painful or tempting to quit. It helps the reader name what is going wrong, judge whether the method is working, decide when to adjust or stop, and cope with resistance or bodily pain. Anything that diagnoses or rescues a stalled or distressing practice serves this part.

parts.heading: Altered States and Intensive Practice
parts.job: Covers deeper, non-ordinary or high-intensity routes into the work, such as psychedelics and similar states: their benefits and traps, what to do with intense experiences, who should be careful, and how to integrate the results. Anything about using or recovering from extreme or altered-state experiences belongs here.

parts.heading: Bringing Reparenting Into Real Life
parts.job: Carries the inner work out into living and relationships: play and preferences, keeping one's own ground among others, finding and trusting people, speaking up and handling conflict, grief and life transitions, and getting outside help. Anything about practicing with and among real people and a real life, rather than inside oneself, serves this part.

parts.heading: Conclusion and Appendix
parts.job: Closes the guide with a final reassurance, then offers background for the curious: how the approach compares to other therapies, where it came from, and what to read next. Anything that wraps up, or places the method in its wider context and lineage, belongs here and is not needed to practice.

roles.name: Protecting and Building Trust With Your Little One
roles.work: The Protector's work: keeping the child safe from harm, whether from outside people, from the reader's own self-attacks or from inherited harsh inner voices, and showing through small, dependable acts of care that the child can rely on the adult. It matters most when warmth is still missing, because it starts the bond with actions and not with feeling. Any passage about defending, setting boundaries for, or earning the trust of the child is this role's work.

roles.name: The Nurturer
roles.work: The Nurturer's work: giving the child love, warmth, comfort and goodwill, and growing the capacity for them when they do not yet come naturally. That includes borrowing love from other people or from a spiritual source, drawing the child in, and widening the sense of what happiness is possible. Any passage about generating, receiving or sustaining affection and joy toward oneself, or about what to do when love will not come, is this role's work.

roles.name: The Inner Guide: Becoming Your Own Shepherd
roles.work: The Guide's work: wisdom, teaching and direction. It chooses what the child learns and experiences, holds standards without harshness, and gives perspective and a healthy sense of timing, limits and imperfection. It can start from borrowed wisdom or hindsight. Any passage about judgment, discipline, learning, guidance or balancing indulgence with firmness is this role's work.
